name: QuickSigner
summary: Legally binding e-signatures with unlimited documents and no per-envelope caps: send a secure link and recipients sign from any device without creating an account. ISO/IEC 27001-certified, AATL signatures, valid across the US, UK and EU; a fair-priced DocuSign alternative.
best_for: cost-conscious teams that want certified e-signing (ISO 27001, AATL) with unlimited documents from ~$5/mo and a real free tier
skip_if: you need advanced workflow features and integrations of the big suites: this wins on price, not on integration depth
honest_knock: The price is the argument, and the legal ceiling is the limit. QuickSigner's own llms.txt says it issues Advanced, not Qualified, Electronic Signatures, and names its weaker fit plainly: organisations needing QES, contract lifecycle management with redlining and analytics, or on-premise deployment. Below that line it does what it says for a fraction of per-envelope pricing, and there is a free plan (Personal, 5 documents a month): recipients sign from a link with no account, app or token. A few users report occasional email-deliverability hiccups, which weighs more here than usual because the emailed link is the whole signing route.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month ($48/yr), unlimited documents
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17, re-read 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-20, and read again on 2026-11-13 on QuickSigner's redesigned pricing page) Free, shown as 'Personal Plan (free)' inside the app: 5 documents a month, 3 signers and 1 document per request, PDF up to 5 MB, signature and stamp fields, certificate and diploma sealing, and uploads from Google Drive. Business is $5 per user a month ($48 a year, so $4 a month billed yearly) and is where documents become unlimited: 10 signers and 3 documents per request, PDF or Word up to 10 MB, 10 reusable templates, signing order, reminders, a saved signature, and search, filters, tags and reports. Professional is $15 per user a month ($144 a year): 50 signers and 10 documents per request, 15 MB, unlimited templates, OTP verification by SMS or WhatsApp, editing a request after sending, bulk send, teams, priority support and the eSignature API. Enterprise is priced on a custom quote for high API volume, custom approval flows and large teams. Annual billing saves 20%, and Business and Professional carry a 14-day free trial. The API has a free developer account with unlimited test requests; going live requires Professional, which includes the first 50 production sign requests free, then $0.30 per request, with a lower rate above 500 requests a month. llms.txt adds that completed test documents are watermarked. ISO/IEC 27001:2022-certified and AATL, legally binding under the ESIGN Act, UETA and eIDAS.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 5 and 16 November 2026 the session tested QuickSigner twice on one account: on 5 November the Personal (free) plan up to the upload screen, and on 16 November the Pro plan, provided by the vendor, from upload to a signed document with download, certificate, template and the cancel route. Nothing was paid, cancelled or deleted. On 16 November the Pro plan was used end to end for one request, signed by our own test address; nothing went to a third party. Upload: the kit file attachment-AIBM-002.pdf was shown as attachment_AIBM_002.pdf, so the hyphen to underscore change seen on 5 November on the free plan also happens on Pro; the list shows attachment_AIBM_002 and the download is named attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf. The upload step also offers Merge into a single document, and the sources Upload file and Google Drive. Fields: Signatures and other fields, Edit, opens Add and edit fields with the types Signature, Text, Checkbox, Date, Initials, Paragraph, File and Stamp (after More...). A Signature field was dragged onto the page, the signer was assigned automatically, Mandatory was on and Fixed was off, and the form then said You have 1 signatures. There is also an Extract button, which was not used. Signing yourself: I am also signing was switched on with only our own test address (an empty second signer row was ignored). Send at 22:13:28 CET (21:13:28 UTC) went straight to the sign page, which said You have to sign in 1 place(s). Start, a click on the field and Select signature type offered Draw, Upload image and Text; we chose Text, typed a short test text, Save and Send. The message was You have successfully signed!. Signed at 21:14:04 UTC and completed at 21:14:05 UTC, so sending to signed took about 37 seconds, and from the upload to signed about 1.5 minutes. The list then showed the status Completed. Download and audit trail: the detail window (the three dots) shows Completed, a sent date of 11/16/2026 22:13, a completed date of 11/16/2026 22:14, the signer marked Signed, a separate Certificate Download link and a Download button. The two downloads were the signed PDF (attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf, 315 KB, 2 pages: the original plus an extra page) and the certificate (Certificate_attachment_AIBM_002.pdf). The Certificate Of Completion lists COMPLETED, the document name, the signature request ID, the number of signers, the sender email, SENT ON and COMPLETED ON in UTC, SENT VIA WEB and per signer an ID, email, SIGN DATE, IP ADDRESS and USER AGENT, the completed field (Signature) and Digitally signed by QuickSigner.com. Seal: the signed PDF has a real sign field named Signature1 with a ByteRange and a Reason that starts with QuickSigner.com ID, and the visible text Digitally sealed by QuickSigner.com. A closer check of the signed file by the coordinating session found two PAdES signatures with the SubFilter ETSI.CAdES.detached; the certificate is issued to Innovoris Labs Srl by DigitalSign CA G1 under DigitalSign Global Root RSA CA. AATL is not mentioned in the interface or in the certificate text, and we did not check whether the certificate chain is trusted by the Adobe approved trust list, so we make no claim about it. Templates: on Pro, Templates, New template and Create template work (upload, a role Signer in place of an email address, fields optional); the page said Successfully saved! and the row has the buttons Edit, Bulk send and Use. Bulk send was not used. The template attachment_AIBM_002 stays in the account. On 5 November the same page on the free plan said Available only with a Business plan. Word and Excel: the hidden file picker accepts application/pdf, application/msword, the docx type, application/vnd.ms-excel and the xlsx type, so PDF, Word (doc and docx) and Excel (xls and xlsx) are accepted by the interface; no .docx file was actually uploaded. Cancel route: My Account on Pro has only Compare plans (a link to the price section of the vendor site), 2FA Enable, API Enable, Notifications, Consent screen and Delete Account. There is no button to stop or downgrade Pro or to manage billing. Nothing was clicked. From 5 November on the free plan: the kit file attachment-AIBM-001.pdf was also shown as attachment_AIBM_001.pdf, and without a signer the page said You must fill in at least one signer and Send stayed greyed out; nothing was sent on that day. The test objects stay in the account: the signed request and the template. No API key was created and no support message was sent.
exit_test.awkward: There is no visible way to stop or downgrade Pro in My Account, only Compare plans and Delete Account, and uploaded file names change from hyphens to underscores.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 and 16 November 2026 on one account: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 5 November we used the free Personal plan up to the upload screen. By 16 November the same account showed Pro, provided by the vendor, so we did not buy it and saw no checkout. On Pro we sent one request to our own test address, signed it ourselves and downloaded the signed PDF and the certificate. Nothing went to a third party. On 19 November 2026 we rechecked the signatures in the signed PDF and the pricing page.
findings: Sending to signed took 37 seconds on Pro (sent 21:13:28 UTC, signed 21:14:04 UTC, completed 21:14:05 UTC), and about 1.5 minutes from upload. With 'I am also signing' switched on, Send went straight to the sign page. The signature type was Draw, Upload image or Text; we chose Text.

The field editor offers Signature, Text, Checkbox, Date, Initials, Paragraph, File and Stamp (the last ones after 'More...'). The signer was assigned automatically; Mandatory was on and Fixed was off.

The download is the signed PDF (attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf, 315 KB, 2 pages: the original plus an extra page) and a separate Certificate of Completion. The certificate lists the request ID, sender email, sent and completed times in UTC, 'sent via web', and per signer the email, sign date, IP address and user agent.

The signed PDF carries two PAdES signatures (SubFilter ETSI.CAdES.detached): a seal from QuickSigner itself and the signer's own signature. Both carry the signing time 21:14:04 UTC inside the file, but neither holds a separate trusted timestamp from a timestamp authority. The certificate is issued to Innovoris Labs Srl by DigitalSign CA G1 and chains to DigitalSign Global Root RSA CA. The pricing page lists AATL document sealing, but the app and the certificate do not mention AATL, and we did not open the file in Adobe Acrobat to see whether it validates there, so we make no claim about it (rechecked 19 November 2026).

Templates: on Personal the Templates page said 'Available only with a Business plan'. On Pro, New template worked (upload, a role 'Signer' instead of an email address, fields optional) and saved with Edit, Bulk send and Use. We did not test the Business plan itself.

An uploaded file name changes: attachment-AIBM-001.pdf (free, 5 Nov) and attachment-AIBM-002.pdf (Pro, 16 Nov) were shown with underscores instead of hyphens, and the signed download carries the underscore name. We compared display names only, not file contents.

The upload step offers 'Merge into a single document' and the sources 'Upload file' and 'Google Drive'. The file picker accepts PDF, Word and Excel types; we did not upload a .docx, so conversion is untested.

My Account on Pro shows only 'Compare plans', 2FA, API, Notifications, Consent screen and 'Delete Account'. We found no button to stop or downgrade Pro or to manage billing. Nothing was clicked; a route through support or a billing email may exist.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 5 and 16 November 2026 the session tested QuickSigner twice on one account: on 5 November the Personal (free) plan up to the upload screen, and on 16 November the Pro plan, provided by the vendor, from upload to a signed document with download, certificate, template and the cancel route. Nothing was paid, cancelled or deleted. On 16 November the Pro plan was used end to end for one request, signed by our own test address; nothing went to a third party. Upload: the kit file attachment-AIBM-002.pdf was shown as attachment_AIBM_002.pdf, so the hyphen to underscore change seen on 5 November on the free plan also happens on Pro; the list shows attachment_AIBM_002 and the download is named attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf. The upload step also offers Merge into a single document, and the sources Upload file and Google Drive. Fields: Signatures and other fields, Edit, opens Add and edit fields with the types Signature, Text, Checkbox, Date, Initials, Paragraph, File and Stamp (after More...). A Signature field was dragged onto the page, the signer was assigned automatically, Mandatory was on and Fixed was off, and the form then said You have 1 signatures. There is also an Extract button, which was not used. Signing yourself: I am also signing was switched on with only our own test address (an empty second signer row was ignored). Send at 22:13:28 CET (21:13:28 UTC) went straight to the sign page, which said You have to sign in 1 place(s). Start, a click on the field and Select signature type offered Draw, Upload image and Text; we chose Text, typed a short test text, Save and Send. The message was You have successfully signed!. Signed at 21:14:04 UTC and completed at 21:14:05 UTC, so sending to signed took about 37 seconds, and from the upload to signed about 1.5 minutes. The list then showed the status Completed. Download and audit trail: the detail window (the three dots) shows Completed, a sent date of 11/16/2026 22:13, a completed date of 11/16/2026 22:14, the signer marked Signed, a separate Certificate Download link and a Download button. The two downloads were the signed PDF (attachment_AIBM_002_signed.pdf, 315 KB, 2 pages: the original plus an extra page) and the certificate (Certificate_attachment_AIBM_002.pdf). The Certificate Of Completion lists COMPLETED, the document name, the signature request ID, the number of signers, the sender email, SENT ON and COMPLETED ON in UTC, SENT VIA WEB and per signer an ID, email, SIGN DATE, IP ADDRESS and USER AGENT, the completed field (Signature) and Digitally signed by QuickSigner.com. Seal: the signed PDF has a real sign field named Signature1 with a ByteRange and a Reason that starts with QuickSigner.com ID, and the visible text Digitally sealed by QuickSigner.com. A closer check of the signed file by the coordinating session found two PAdES signatures with the SubFilter ETSI.CAdES.detached; the certificate is issued to Innovoris Labs Srl by DigitalSign CA G1 under DigitalSign Global Root RSA CA. AATL is not mentioned in the interface or in the certificate text, and we did not check whether the certificate chain is trusted by the Adobe approved trust list, so we make no claim about it. Templates: on Pro, Templates, New template and Create template work (upload, a role Signer in place of an email address, fields optional); the page said Successfully saved! and the row has the buttons Edit, Bulk send and Use. Bulk send was not used. The template attachment_AIBM_002 stays in the account. On 5 November the same page on the free plan said Available only with a Business plan. Word and Excel: the hidden file picker accepts application/pdf, application/msword, the docx type, application/vnd.ms-excel and the xlsx type, so PDF, Word (doc and docx) and Excel (xls and xlsx) are accepted by the interface; no .docx file was actually uploaded. Cancel route: My Account on Pro has only Compare plans (a link to the price section of the vendor site), 2FA Enable, API Enable, Notifications, Consent screen and Delete Account. There is no button to stop or downgrade Pro or to manage billing. Nothing was clicked. From 5 November on the free plan: the kit file attachment-AIBM-001.pdf was also shown as attachment_AIBM_001.pdf, and without a signer the page said You must fill in at least one signer and Send stayed greyed out; nothing was sent on that day. The test objects stay in the account: the signed request and the template. No API key was created and no support message was sent.
exit_test.awkward: There is no visible way to stop or downgrade Pro in My Account, only Compare plans and Delete Account, and uploaded file names change from hyphens to underscores.
